title: Objects and Event Records
summary: Group related facts into objects, read and update properties, and combine objects inside arrays.

sketchBlocks.title: An object names the facts that belong to one thing
A const object can still have changing properties
Arrays and objects work together
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
Real programs often need many structured records. Put objects inside an array when you need a collection of things that share the same kinds of properties.

```js
const events = [
  { name: "Jazz Night", room: "Music Center" },
  { name: "Robotics Lab", room: "Engineering Hall" }
];

console.log(events[1].name);
```

Line by line:

1. `events` is an array with two items.
2. Each item is an object with `name` and `room` properties.
3. `events[1]` reads the second object.
4. `.name` then reads the `name` property from that object.

This combination—**array of objects**—becomes the main data shape for the rest of the course.

quizDraft.title: Read a property
quizDraft.prompt: Given `const book = { title: "Dawn", pages: 240 };`, which expression reads the title?
quizDraft.hint: Look for the object name followed by a known property name.

help.concept: Dot notation reads a named property from an object.
help.hint_1: The object is `book`; the property is `title`.
help.hint_2: Choose the expression that connects those names with a dot.

quizDraft.title: Reason about object records
quizDraft.prompt: Which statements are true? Select all that apply.
quizDraft.hint: Distinguish object properties from array positions.

help.concept: Objects use named properties; const keeps the binding stable but does not freeze every property.
help.hint_1: A property name such as `.score` is different from an array index.
help.hint_2: Reject the statement that treats every object like an indexed array.

options: An object can group several related facts.
A property can be read with dot notation.
A property of a const object can be reassigned.
An object automatically has numeric array indexes.

quizDraft.title: Complete a property update
quizDraft.prompt: Choose the property name that changes the player's score.
quizDraft.hint: Use the property that represents the value being changed.

help.concept: Dot notation places the property name after the object name.
help.hint_1: The assignment target should describe the player's numeric result.
help.hint_2: Choose the property whose meaning matches the new value `18`.

quizDraft.title: Trace a record update
quizDraft.prompt: Arrange the steps for changing one property and observing it.
quizDraft.hint: The object must exist before one of its properties can change.

help.concept: Think from record creation to one targeted update.
help.hint_1: The changed value belongs to a property on the existing object.
help.hint_2: Observe the property only after the assignment has happened.

tokens: Read the property you want to change
correctOrder: Read the property you want to change

quizDraft.title: Create a book record
quizDraft.prompt: Problem: A library system needs the title, author, and page count to travel together as one book record instead of as unrelated variables. Task: Create `book` with `title`, `author`, and `pages` properties, then log the title and page count. Expected result: the Console shows values read from the same object.
quizDraft.hint: Keep all three facts inside one object.

help.concept: An object groups related values under named properties.
help.hint_1: Use an object literal assigned to `book`.
help.hint_2: Read `book.title` and `book.pages` when you log the result.

quizDraft.title: Update a game character
quizDraft.prompt: Problem: A game character's health belongs to that character record and must change when the character takes damage. Task: Create `player` with `name` and `health`. Reduce `player.health` by 20, then log the updated health. Expected result: the Console shows the reduced health value from the player object.
quizDraft.hint: Keep the same object and change only one property.

help.concept: A property inside a const object can still be updated.
help.hint_1: Start health at a numeric value large enough to subtract 20.
help.hint_2: Assign `player.health - 20` back to `player.health` before logging it.

quizDraft.title: Read from a product catalog
quizDraft.prompt: Problem: A product catalog contains multiple products with the same data shape, and the storefront needs to read one product from the collection. Task: Create `products` as an array of two objects with `name` and `price` properties. Log the name of the second product. Expected result: the Console shows the second product's name.
quizDraft.hint: Read the array item first, then its property.

help.concept: Arrays can hold structured objects, and indexing can select one record before dot notation reads a property.
help.hint_1: The collection should contain two object literals.
help.hint_2: Use the second array position, then `.name`.
